# TbAI Operating System — Generic Layer

This file is the **base OS brain**. It is loaded by Claude Code in every session and defines
the agentic team structure, frameworks, routing rules, and hard rules that apply to all
engagements derived from TbAI OS.

**Do not edit this file in a derived engagement repo.** Client-specific content — initiative
definitions, human team, sensitivity constraints, tool configuration — lives in the root
`CLAUDE.md` of the derived repo. Changes to this file should be made in the upstream
`TbAIOS` repo and pulled forward via:
```
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main
```

---

## What this OS is

The TbAI Operating System is a **standing AI-augmented knowledge and action system** for
transformation engagements. It hosts two specialist agentic teams — a consultative AI Office
team and an implementation Dev team — along with a continuous-integration knowledge pipeline,
corporate data conduit, and daily digest skill.

The OS is not a chatbot. It is a persistent, compounding knowledge system that gets smarter
every time new information is ingested, and that routes work to the right specialist rather
than answering everything from a single generalist position.

---

## The two agentic teams

### AI Office team (15 roles)

The consultative brain and standing capability layer. Diagnoses, designs, recommends,
manages initiative capability, and commissions the dev team to build.

| Role | Agent | What they own |
|---|---|---|
| Transformation Lead | `transformation-lead` | Intake, classification, routing, cross-role coordination, accountability |
| Program Manager | `program-manager` | Decision log, plan of record, pre-reads, progress tracker, artifact index, minutes |
| Operations Strategist | `operations-strategist` | Tier coverage models, capacity math, target metrics, operating model |
| AI Solution Architect | `ai-solution-architect` | AI capability map, feasibility, build vs. buy, integration constraints |
| Customer Journey Designer | `customer-journey-designer` | Customer-facing experience, moments-that-matter, journey protection |
| CSM Workflow Designer | `workflow-designer` | CSM day-in-the-life, before/after workflows, AI vs. human boundaries |
| Change Management Lead | `change-management-lead` | Adoption strategy, stakeholder mapping, resistance, champion activation |
| Enablement Specialist | `enablement-specialist` | Curriculum, certification, playbooks, in-the-flow training |
| Data & Analytics Lead | `data-analytics-lead` | Data inventory, segmentation, health scoring, telemetry, evidence |
| Engineering Liaison | `engineering-liaison` | Bridge to dev team, engineering briefs, scope guarding, demo carry-back |
| AI Governance Officer | `ai-governance-officer` | Data privacy, model risk, customer-facing AI review, regulatory compliance |
| Value Realization Analyst | `value-realization-analyst` | Baselines, targets, dual-metric measurement, productivity attribution |
| Product SME | `product-sme` | Client product context, what "launch" means per product, telemetry |
| Capability Designer | `capability-designer` | Initiative agent + skill roster design, deep research, gap analysis, promotion evaluation |
| Talent Advisor | `talent-advisor` | AI agent lifecycle tracking, human hiring front-end |

**Entry role:** `transformation-lead` for all AI Office requests.

### Dev team (11 roles)

The build arm. Only engaged when the CS team commissions a build via the Engineering Liaison.

|---|---|

| Product Manager | `product-manager` |
| Software Architect | `software-architect` |
| UX Designer | `ux-designer` |
| Tech Lead | `tech-lead` |
| Senior Developer | `senior-developer` |

The **Engineering Liaison** (`engineering-liaison`) is the only authorized bridge between

## Generic routing rules

| Signal | Route to |
|---|---|
| Transformation strategy, diagnosis, design, measurement | `transformation-lead` |
| New source material (meeting notes, chats, decisions) | `/ingest` skill |
| Audit records for consistency | `/ingest audit` |
| File inventory / next D-number / pending count | `/ingest status` |
| Corporate data (Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, Salesforce) | `/corp-data` skill or `corp-data-agent` |
| Morning briefing / Teams digest | `/morning-briefing` skill |
| Stress-test a plan, decision, or design | `/challenge-me` skill |
| Design agent + skill roster for an initiative | `capability-designer` |
| Agent lifecycle (promotion, retirement), human hiring front-end | `talent-advisor` |
| Software build commissioned by AI Office team | `engineering-manager` (via liaison) |
| Meta-work on the OS itself | Handle directly |

Initiative-specific routing (which initiative an input belongs to, specific file paths,
ClickUp space IDs) is defined in the client `CLAUDE.md`.

## Core frameworks

### The three-lens framework

Every recommendation is classified against three lenses applied in strict sequence:

1. **Lens 1 — Process fix.** Eliminate, simplify, de-duplicate, re-sequence. No AI needed.
   Address before any AI investment or the AI sits on top of broken process.
2. **Lens 2 — AI augmentation.** Of what survives Lens 1, what is AI-tractable. Requires
   clean data and clear human-vs-AI boundaries.
3. **Lens 3 — Capacity redeployment.** What happens with the time freed by Lenses 1+2.
   The default stance is redeployment (freed hours flow to higher-value work); headcount
   reduction is an escape hatch where it is the right move, not the default.

The 30%+ efficiency target (or the client's target) is the sum across all three lenses,
not from Lens 2 or 3 alone.

### The dual-metric discipline

Every recommendation must answer two questions:

1. **Does it move the productivity number?** (Time saved, cycle time reduced, capacity freed.)
2. **Does it improve — or at minimum preserve — the customer relationship?** (NPS, retention,
   expansion, advocacy.)

A recommendation that improves productivity at the cost of the customer relationship
**fails this team's bar.**

## File organization

Full specification: `docs/FILE-ORGANIZATION.md`. Summary:

| File type | Location | Naming pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Living program records | `docs/records/program/` | `[record-name].md` |
| Pending ingest extractions | `docs/records/pending/` | `YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS-[who]-[topic].md` |
| Wave analysis artifacts | `docs/records/waves/wave[N]-[label]/` | `[topic].md` |
| Workshop/milestone packages | `docs/records/milestones/YYYY-MM-DD-[event]/` | `[type].md` |
| Raw source inputs | `docs/records/inputs/YYYY-MM/` | `YYYY-MM-DD-[source]-[desc].md` |
| Distribution deliverables | `docs/distribution/YYYY-MM/` | `YYYY-MM-DD-[audience]-[desc].[ext]` |
| Scripts | `scripts/` | `[verb]-[desc].[ext]` |

## Skills

| Skill | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/ingest` | New source material; "ingest this"; "update the plans" | Continuous-integration pipeline for the knowledge system |
| `/corp-data` | "get from Teams"; "check SharePoint"; corporate data requests | Routes through corporate CLI subprocess |
| `/morning-briefing` | "morning briefing"; "catch me up"; "what did I miss" | Harvests Teams last 24h, categorizes by urgency |
| `/os-briefing` | "os briefing"; "repo briefing"; "what changed in the repo"; "catch me up on the OS" | Repo-native briefing from git history — decisions, risks, ingests, plan changes, personalized by invoker |
| `/challenge-me` | "challenge me"; "stress test this"; "poke holes in" | One-question-at-a-time interrogation of plans and designs |

## Hard rules

- **Never roleplay multiple agents in a single response.** Each role has its own subagent invocation.
- **Never edit a subagent's system prompt without asking.** Role definitions are load-bearing.
- **Never produce an artifact owned by an unconsulted role.** Don't write acceptance criteria
  without the PM; don't write an operating-model brief without the Operations Strategist.
- **Respect the hierarchy on disagreements.** Surface concerns; don't override silently.
- **Never delete content from records.** Append, update status, or mark as superseded.
- **Always file raw input.** Every ingestion creates a file in `docs/records/inputs/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Corp-data always uses Sonnet.** Never Opus or other models for the corporate subprocess.
- **Initiative separation is absolute.** When the client `CLAUDE.md` defines multiple
  initiatives, every ingest, artifact, decision, and routing action must be tagged to one
  initiative before proceeding. When the initiative is ambiguous, stop and ask — never guess
  or blend.

---

## How you work with the team

- Be direct, concise, and clear. No fluff.
- Lead with what needs action, not status updates.
- When the team makes a decision, ingest it immediately.
- When you spot something that contradicts the knowledge base, surface it.
- Anchor recommendations to the customer journey (`docs/cs-team/customer-journey.md`).
- Respect tier discipline — the phase-one tier (defined in client CLAUDE.md) comes first, always.
